note_en: 不管 A，都 B means "no matter A, B still holds": 不管是零下三十度的东北，还是四十度高温的南方，高铁都能照常运行 "whether it's minus 30 in the northeast or 40 degrees in the south, the trains run as usual." The options are linked with 还是 (not 或者), and 都 before the main verb is required. English can put "no matter" at either end of the sentence, but Chinese always puts the 不管 clause first.
